subject: Interactive delivery lag — customer action plan and temporary fallbacks
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Verma <amit.verma@clearwavelabs.com>, Clara Zhou <clara.zhou@clearwavelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interactive delivery lag — initial notice and short-term mitigations

Hi Amit / Clara,

Quick note to confirm we saw the elevated delivery latency on your interactive/chat routes beginning ~08:50 PT this morning. We're treating this as a priority and currently triaging in parallel across the serving and edge teams.

Impact we've observed so far:
- Increased per-token latency for streaming responses on route /v1/chat/stream (p50 ~180ms -> ~600ms)
- Customer-visible pauses in long responses (users report small stalls every ~5–10s)
- No evidence of direct data corruption or missing tokens; responses complete but with degraded interactivity

Short-term mitigations we're implementing now (expected minutes):
1) Route traffic for your critical production key (ClearWave-prod) to a lower-utilization pool in us-west-2 (canary shift) — this should reduce tail latency while we diagnose.
2) Enable conservative batching window for your key to prioritize latency over throughput (temporary config change).
3) Apply a non-disruptive restart to a small set of serving pods to reset KV cache behavior where we see backpressure.

Action requested from ClearWave for faster recovery:
- If possible, reduce concurrent long-response sessions by 15–20% for the next 1–2 hours (helps slope the load while we shift capacity).

I'll update you in 30–45 minutes with telemetry and expected recovery time. Attaching a brief trace export and an impact matrix for internal use.

Thanks,
Camila
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference


From: Amit Verma <amit.verma@clearwavelabs.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clara Zhou <clara.zhou@clearwavelabs.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interactive delivery lag — initial notice and short-term mitigations

Camila — thanks for the quick heads-up. We can throttle one of our ingestion workers to drop ~20% of concurrent sessions for the next 90 minutes; I'll coordinate with engineering now.

Two quick questions:
1) Will the canary shift impact any data residency or routing (we need to confirm logs go to the same S3 bucket)?
2) If you enable conservative batching, should our client SDK change any retry logic?

Appreciate the trace — we’re standing by for your next update.

— Amit
Sr. Platform Engineer, ClearWave Labs


From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Verma <amit.verma@clearwavelabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interactive delivery lag — initial notice and short-term mitigations

Team — quick status update from infra: canary shift completed at 10:40 PT, and key-level p50 latency for ClearWave-prod has improved to ~220ms; tail remains elevated (p95 ~980ms).

Diagnostics summary so far:
- Root cause hypothesis: transient backpressure in edge proxies combined with a KV-cache sync stall on a subset of older serving instances (instances running runtime v1.8.1 show higher FIM latency).
- Evidence: trace g-7f3b2 shows repeated retry windows between edge->serving hops at 08:50–09:15, correlated with a backlog spike in queue metrics.

Planned next steps (today):
A) Roll forward a targeted runtime patch to affected instances (non-breaking, no model reload) — ETA 2 hours.
B) Add a short-term client SDK guidance for ClearWave: reduce client-side token-chunk size to 512 tokens (from 1024) to avoid chunking stalls and reduce perceived pauses.
C) Postmortem to follow with timeline and permanent fixes (likely runtime patch + edge backpressure controls).

Camila: I drafted the client guidance note below — please send to ClearWave if you’re comfortable.

--- draft SDK guidance ---
If you observe stalls during streaming responses, temporarily set your SDK chunk_size to 512 and increase your client-side receive timeout to 45s. If you use long responses (>2k tokens), consider breaking into shorter assistant turns. These changes are reversible once we finish the runtime rollout.

Ben
Staff Engineer, Runtime


From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Verma <amit.verma@clearwavelabs.com>, Clara Zhou <clara.zhou@clearwavelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-10T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: recovery summary, customer actions, and next steps (post-incident)

Hi Amit / Clara,

Thanks again for your patience while we worked through the delivery degradation. This note summarizes what happened, the immediate mitigations we applied, and recommended next steps for ClearWave before we close the loop.

What happened (summary):
- On 2026-09-09 08:50 PT we observed backpressure in edge proxies that amplified token emission latency for streaming/chat on your production key. A subset of serving pods (runtime v1.8.1) also showed a KV-cache sync stall that increased request tail latency.
- Visible customer impact: longer pauses during multi-thousand-token replies; median response completion was intact but interactivity suffered for ~2.5 hours.

What we changed (mitigations applied):
- 10:40 PT — Canary traffic shift to lower-utilization pool in us-west-2 (reduced p50 from ~600ms to ~220ms).
- 11:10 PT — Targeted restart and runtime patch rollout to affected serving instances (resolved KV-cache stalls).
- 11:45 PT — Temporary conservative batching configuration for your key (lower batching window).
- SDK guidance issued to reduce client chunk_size to 512 tokens and extend receive timeout to 45s (temporary).

Customer action items (recommended):
1) Implement SDK temporary changes (chunk_size=512, receive timeout=45s) for next 24–48 hours while we complete longer-term fixes.
2) If you have an automated canary traffic test, add an interactive-response test that sends 4–6 long-turn requests (3–4k tokens) once per hour during your peak window — this will help detect regressions.
3) Share any user sessions where you still see stalls; attach session IDs and approximate timestamps so we can cross-reference traces.

Planned permanent fixes from Redwood:
- Upgrade all serving pools to runtime v1.9.x with improved KV sync logic (scheduled next week).
- Harden edge proxy backpressure throttles to avoid amplification during short spikes.
- Add per-key backpressure telemetry to surface these issues before user-visible impact.

We recognize the disruption this caused for some of your interactive flows. As a goodwill gesture we’re proposing a one-time credit for impacted usage; Marissa from CS will follow up on the details.

Next call? If you’d like, we can do a short 30-minute post-incident review tomorrow to run through traces and action owners. Proposed times: 09:00 PT or 13:00 PT.

Apologies again, and we’ll keep you posted as we complete the runtime upgrades.

Warmly,
Camila
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
